title: Private Deploy CI/CD & Release Mechanics — draft
content:
Purpose
This document captures a working draft of the CI/CD and release mechanics for private deployments (VPC and on-prem) — focusing on Helm/OCI charts, GitOps (ArgoCD/Argo Rollouts), Terraform module expectations, image signing and provenance, and special air-gap/offline flows. The goal: a repeatable, auditable, secure path from merge -> signed artifact -> promoted image -> GitOps-driven deployment with safe rollback/fallback.

Audience
- Platform engineers implementing private deployment automation
- Release engineers coordinating upgrades for customer private stacks
- Solutions and SEs who onboard customers into private model serving

Scope / Non‑Scope
- Scope: CI pipelines, image provenance, chart packaging, Argo apps, Terraform module notes (VPC + registry infra), upgrade strategies (canary/rolling/blue-green), air-gap mechanics.
- Non-scope: model packaging, per-model inference code changes, customer-specific network design beyond standard Terraform modules.

High-level flow (ideal)
1) Build -> SBOM: CI builds images (builder pool), produce SBOM (syft) and metadata.
2) Sign: Sign images and attach signatures/attestations (cosign + Rekor, optional Notation) with a key stored in HSM/KMS (or offline key for air-gap).
3) Publish: Push to canonical OCI registry (hosted or customer private registry). Tagging convention: stable (channel), semver+buildmeta, and sha256 tag.
4) Promote -> GitOps: When release criteria pass (smoke tests, integration), CI updates the GitOps repo (app-of-apps pattern) with the exact image digests and Helm chart OCI reference. ArgoCD sync picks up the change and starts rollout.
5) Rollout & Observability: Use Argo Rollouts (canary) + metrics gating (latency/error) and automatic analysis. If failure, automatic rollback to previous digest.
6) Audit: All artifacts (SBOM, signature, promotion logs, terraform run ids) are stored and linked to the release record.

Key CI primitives and recommendations
- Builders: ephemeral build agents in customer VPC (self-hosted runners) for air-gapped installs; otherwise shared hosted runners that can push to custody registries via short-lived credentials.
- SBOMs: generate SBOMs for each image (syft) and attach to release. SBOM should be published to the artifact store (S3/GCS with restricted ACLs) and referenced in the release metadata.
- Signing: cosign is our default. Sign both image and chart artifacts. Push signatures to Rekor transparency log. For HSM/KMS integration, use cosign KMS support; for air-gap, support offline signing with detached signatures transported via artifact bundle.
- Attestations: Use in-toto or Grafeas/Attestation for CI test results (unit, integration, acceptance). Store attestations alongside SBOMs.

Helm & chart mechanics
- Chart packaging: prefer Helm v3 OCI charts. Charts should be immutable and referenced by digest (oci://registry/namespace/chart@sha256:...).
- Values: enforce a minimal values schema and template tests (helm unittest or chart-testing). Charts must include upgrade hooks with idempotency guards.
- Chart signing: sign chart archive with cosign; upload signature to same registry. Document requirement: charts without signature fail promotion.
- Chart-Image coupling: charts should not float image tags; instead charts accept image.digest and image.repository as values (we auto-inject exact digest at promotion time).

GitOps repo layout (recommended)
- app-of-apps root repo: apps/<env>/<customer>/<service>/kustomization.yaml or helmRelease manifest referencing OCI chart by digest.
- promotion CI updates a tiny PR (or direct commit via robot) to the appropriate env branch: set chart/image digests + chart values patch.
- Protect branches with required checks (signed commits, CI status, approver).
- ArgoCD: single cluster per customer mapping, use app-of-apps so operator can promote multiple clusters consistently.

Argo Rollouts / Canary strategy
- Canary baseline: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated metric analysis windows (default 10m). Metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, token-cost regressions (if instrumentation).
- Automated pause points require analysis pass or manual approval if risk label present.
- Fallback: immediate automatic rollback on SLO breach or missing readiness. Keep at least N previous revisions kept for fast rollback.

Terraform module notes (VPC + infra)
- Module boundaries: networking (vpc/subnets/route-tables/nat), registry infra (ECR/Artifact Registry + replication), IAM (roles, service accounts), cluster bootstrap (k8s cluster + node pools), observability (prometheus remote write endpoints, log sinks).
- State backend: remote state in S3/GCS with locking (DynamoDB/CloudSQL lock). For on-prem customer-managed backend, provide recommended configs and migration guides.
- Inputs: make module accept CIDR blocks, allowed CIDR for ingress from Redwood control-plane, bastion config, private endpoint toggles. Keep minimal outputs: registry endpoint, service account names, or Kubeconfig endpoint if managed.
- Terraform run tagging: every apply should generate metadata JSON (git sha, pipeline id, actor) and write to a central audit bucket for release traceability.

Registry and image promotion details
- Canonical registry: hosted or customer-provided. For hosted private stacks we recommend using cross-account ECR with enforced image policy.
- Tagging: <service>-v<semver>+build.<n> and always push digest tag. Promotion updates GitOps repo with digest.
- Mirroring (air-gap): Provide a small mirror tool (skopeo based) that pulls signed artifacts and pushes to customer import registry. Mirror produces a manifest mapping old->new digests and includes signatures and SBOM in the bundle.

Air-gap / offline install mechanics (special flow)
- Build site produces a signed bundle: images (tar), charts (helm package), SBOMs, signatures, attestations, and a manifest file. Artifact bundle is exported to transport media or secure transfer.
- Import site runs customer-side importer (recommended container image) that verifies signatures against a supplied CA/fulcio root and Rekor entries (if reachable) or offline signed root.
- Keys for signing: recommend HSM-backed signing key; for air-gap support offline keys with strict rotation audit. Document manual steps for emergency signing revocation and rekey.

Image signing & provenance (detailed)
- Tools: cosign (default), Rekor, Notation as options.
- KMS/HSM: prefer using customer KMS (Cloud KMS / AWS KMS) with hardware protection for production keys. Provide wrappers for cosign to discover KMS URIs per tenant.
- Validation policy: on target clusters, run admission controller (notary/admission-webhook) that rejects unsigned images or images signed by unknown identities. Alternatively use OPA Gatekeeper with a policy for image signatures and attestations.
- Attestation validation: ensure that required attestations (sbom, tests passed) are present and meet minimum criteria before allowing deployment to a prod channel.

CI/CD pipeline templates (recommendations)
- GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / Tekton recommended templates included in repo: build -> test -> sbom+sign -> push -> promote\.yaml.
- For on-prem: self-hosted runners with ephemeral creds using short-lived tokens from a Vault. Provide a bootstrap script to provision runner and rotate tokens.
- Secrets: store keys in Vault or KMS; restrict access by pipeline role. CI robots should have least privilege S3/registry push roles with just enough permission to upload releases.

Testing & gating
- Pre-promotion gate: unit + integration tests + smoke tests in ephemeral env. Security scan: container vulnerability scanning (Trivy) and SBOM policy.
- Post-deploy test: automated smoke tests run after Argo Rollouts steps; failures trigger rollback.
- Canary analysis: use Prometheus or Datadog metrics integrated into Argo Rollouts analysis templates.

Upgrade playbook (customer-facing upgrade runbook template)
- Pre-upgrade: verify terraform plan (network unchanged), snapshot cluster state/backups, ensure at least 2 successful smoke-run builds on canary channel.
- Day-0: start promotion to staging clusters via GitOps; run full test harness.
- Day-1: promote to 5% prod canary, monitor for 30–60m, if green move to 25% then 100%. If any metric crosses threshold rollback immediately and open incident with required logs.
- Post-upgrade: collect release artifacts (SBOMs, signatures, promotion PR), annotate customer ticket and update release log.

Operational considerations / gotchas
- Time skew & Rekor: Rekor entries assume time-sync between build site and verification site. Air-gap verification must allow signature roots without Rekor check, but require extra manual audit.
- Mutable tags: never rely on floating tags in GitOps; always pin digest.
- Kube admission latency: signature verification in admission path can add overhead; prefer node-level pre-pull+verify for latency-sensitive workloads.
- Terraform drift: baseline drift detection job that warns when terraform remote state deviates from live infra.

Open questions / TODOs
- How tightly do we couple promotion gating to billing metrics (token-cost regressions)? Do we require cost checks on every release?
- Define exact policy for offline signature verification: Rekor optional or required? How to seed Rekor roots in air-gap?
- Decide default canary progression timings and metric thresholds per service-class.
- Document a minimal air-gap acceptance checklist for security/compliance teams.

Appendix: short command snippets / examples
- Inject image digest to Helm values (example): CI will patch values.yaml with image.digest: sha256:<...> and create PR to apps repo.
- Cosign sign: cosign sign --key kms://projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/... gcr.io/my/repo@sha256:<digest>
- Verify example (air-gap offline): cosign verify-blob --key <public.pem> --signature <sig> <image.tar>

Contact
- Primary: Marcus Lee (eng-private-deployments)
- Slack channel: #private-deploys

Notes: This is a working draft intended to converge into the final playbook. Expect follow-ups to add automation templates (GitHub Actions files, terraform module snippets), a packaged mirror tool, and an air-gap importer utility.
